newsitem.title: USA: International Paper sees better EPS ahead.
newsitem.headline: International Paper sees better EPS ahead.

text.p: International Paper said on Tuesday it expected its earnings to increase due to an improved paper pricing environment and steps the company has taken to improve operations, expand capacity and reduce costs.

"Demand continues to improve," said John Dillon, International Paper's chairman and chief executive officer. "Instead of working off excess inventory, customers are ordering based on current business requirements."
Company spokesman Phillip Giaramita told Reuters that recent price increases in container board and bleach board could hold, and pulp pricing also looked firmer.
"We are seeing encouraging signs that inventories are being worked off," he said.

International Paper reported earnings of $0.37 per share for the third quarter of 1996 against $1.27 per share in the same period last year, and Giaramita said poor pricing across most paper grades had depressed results.
"Higher inventories at the start of the year in most paper grades and packaging put pressure on prices, even though sales were roughly the same as the same period last year," Giaramita said.

The company's specialty products division, which includes paper by-products and some non-core chemical and home products business, had earnings during the third quarter of nearly two times the same period last year, he said.
The company said results from the forest products sector were somewhat below the last quarter due mostly to lower timber pricing, but demand in wood products markets improved.
Customer inventories in wood products also continued to trend downwards, the company said.
International Paper said earnings for its printing papers sector improved during the second quarter due to stronger pulp and uncoated paper markets in the United States and Europe.
The sector also benefited from less downtime at U.S. manufacturing facilities, it said.
Pulp prices increased early in the quarter, as did prices last month for reprographics and offset grades, it said.
Price increases also have been announced for the fourth quarter in pulp and uncoated paper grades, the company said.
Packaging profits were down slightly from the previous quarter mainly due to lower containerboard and box prices and weaker results from overseas operations, it said.
But the company said third quarter containerboard volume reached record levels, and a $30-per-ton price increase was announced effective October 1.
Bleached board orders and shipments improved, and price increases of about $40 per ton were announced for U.S. and export markets, it said.

The company has also made several investments that would have a long-term impact, Dillon said. These included increased contributions from former Federal Paper Board businesses now fully integrated into International Paper, the recent acquisition of Forchem, a European specialty chemical company, the start-up of a corrugated packaging plant in the United Kingdom, a spunbond nonwovens line in Mexico, and the pending conversion of a paper machine in Maine to produce coated freesheet.
